text: The filing of a guarantee claim is recorded on the claim row: guarantee_claim.status takes FILED of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and guarantee_claim.filed_at takes the business date of the filing. The submission reference the legacy story records on the case has no field in TSD S3 T3.1 and no case field is read for this key, so no reference element is published in v1 and the screen shows the filing by status and date until the Logical Data Model allocates a field identifier.
why: The legacy acceptance criterion says the submission reference is recorded on the case, and the row the sources define has eight fields of which only filed_at and status can carry a filing; publishing an invented element would put a value in the contract that no field identifier backs.
read: TSD S3 T3.1 (DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022), T3.2 (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS); legacy RWB-E4-014 data table and AC1; FSD S3 A2.2.4.1; LDM v8 has no reference field for a guarantee claim.
confirm: Owner of the guarantee claim in the Logical Data Model and the tech lead of rwb-guarantee
impact: If the reference must be persisted, the row gains a field identifier and a compatible optional element is added at major version 1; until then the reference lives on the TCG channel and the Workbench records the filing, not the reference.

text: The TCG claim channel is INT-29 and has no published interface today, so the submission is the guarantee officer's filing on the channel recorded by the service: no outbound REST call, no file, no queue and no channel callback exists, and the contract declares no channel operation.
why: TSD S3 T5.1 states that INT-29 is not available today and is entered and filed by the guarantee officer, while the FSD and the rules name the channel as an actor and not as a system with an interface; a call or a file invented here would be a dependency no team can satisfy.
read: TSD S3 T5.1 (INT-29), T5.3 (Events None); FSD S3 A2.2 description and integration points; R-GUA-12 and R-GUA-21 systems column (Workbench, TCG claim channel); Architecture v5 slide 8 (outside the cluster).
confirm: Business lead of S3 and the integration owner of rwb-integration
impact: When INT-29 publishes an interface the filing becomes an outbound call or a file with a claim-check, and a new contract dependency and a channel adapter are added; the claim row and the two operations do not change.

text: The seventeen states of the guarantee state machine are case statuses of rwb-case applied by the parent CaseWorkflow from the stage report; the claim row uses the five members of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and this key fixes only one pair of the two vocabularies, PREPARING before the filing and FILED after it.
why: TSD S3 T4 defines the machine over sixteen named states plus seven more, T3.2 defines a five-member claim list, and no source maps one to the other; the split puts the case status with rwb-case, so only the claim row transition belongs to this service.
read: TSD S3 T4 (32 rules over 17 states), T3.2 (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS); FSD S3 A2.2.3.1; Architecture v5 slide 13 (CaseWorkflow parent, child workflow per stage); DP-12.
confirm: Owner of the case status list in rwb-case and the business lead of S3
impact: If a different map is adopted, the claim row takes another member of the list at the filing and the screen shows another word; the case status and the two operations are unchanged.

text: The guarantee service reads the account facts at the ACE batch date through its own SELECT-only views recovery.v_ace_account and recovery.v_ace_batch_status, with no copy kept and no contract dependency on rwb-source-data.
why: DP-05 allows either the rwb-source-data contract or the service's own ACE views, the Work Package records no contract dependency on P1, and Architecture v5 slide 8 states that the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data; the grant to this login is the working read of the split.
read: DP-05 of Template and Rules v5.5 and of the S3 context pack; Architecture v5 slide 8 (30 recovery.v_ace_* views, one login per service); TSD S3 T5.2; legacy RWB-E4-014 data table (v_ace_account, DF-ACE-001 to DF-ACE-042).
confirm: rwb-source-data owner (P1) and the ACE database administrator
impact: If the views must be reached through rwb-source-data's contract, a C dependency on RWB-P1 is added and the read becomes a REST call with a 2 s timeout; the element and the filing are unchanged.

text: The 2 working day timer of R-GUA-12, the 5 working day timer of R-GUA-21 and the claim deadline of R-GUA-01 are durable Temporal timers of the guarantee workflow and case timers written by rwb-case; no timer table is created in rwb_guarantee and the legacy timer rows of DF-WRK-027 to DF-WRK-036 stay with rwb-case.
why: The ownership rows give S3 one table and no job, the target replaces Quartz with Temporal Schedules and durable timers, and the legacy data table lists the shared timer table of the monolith; keeping timer rows in this service would duplicate a case fact.
read: Context pack ownership rows for S3 (one table, no job); Temporal and Drools Design slides 5 and 13; TSD S3 T4 timers column; BRRL v4 R-GUA-12 and R-GUA-21 timer column; TSD S3 T3.1 (no timer field).
confirm: Owner of the case timers in rwb-case and the platform workflow owner
impact: If a timer row is needed in this service, a table and a field set are added to the LDM and the schema before the build; the rules and the two timers do not change.

text: A filing publishes no Kafka event: the ownership rows give S3 no event type, so the signal of a submission is the stage report to the parent CaseWorkflow, delivered as a Temporal signal inside the case; the reporting read that Architecture v5 slide 13 suggests is satisfied by the case and claim state until an event type is catalogued.
why: The two authorities conflict - the ownership rows give S3 zero events, the connection matrix shows rwb-reporting listening to S3 - and this story needs no outbox row, so the smaller reading is taken and the conflict is recorded rather than resolved by inventing an event name.
read: Context pack ownership rows for S3 (Events: 0); Architecture v5 slide 13 row S3 and row P9; TSD S3 T5.3 (Events None); DP-09 and DP-14 of Template and Rules v5.5.
confirm: Owner of the Kafka topic catalogue and the reporting owner (P9)
impact: If an event is catalogued, the service gains the outbox and inbox library dependency RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, one event name under rwb.guarantee.events.v1 and a reporting consumer; nothing else changes.

text: The 409 of PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId} means the claim is already in FILED; the update is idempotent on the claim, the rule version and the status, so a repeated filing answers the first result and writes nothing, and the business text of the 409 is left to the C1 message catalogue.
why: TSD S3 T-A.2 fixes 409 among the error statuses of both operations and gives the update no idempotency header, while the legacy story and the FSD name no conflict case and no message id; a second filing must not create a second filing or move the case twice.
read: TSD S3 T-A.2 (errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503; idempotency not applicable on the PATCH), T3.2 (LOV-CLAIM-STATUS); legacy RWB-E4-014 validation table; FSD S3 A2.2.4.3.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-guarantee and the platform API owner
impact: A different conflict rule changes the status the update answers and the message the officer sees; the elements, the table and the two operations are unchanged.

text: The FSD S3 v3 and TSD S3 v2 status In review is treated as no approval stop: the two stories start on Day 1 at status Draft (realignment v1), and no sign-off is waited for.
why: This run has no human verification stop (U8, D-RCV-60) and a missing approval is an assumption, not a blocker; the source documents carry In review and no approval date for this key.
read: FSD S3 v3 document control (Status In review); TSD S3 v2 document control (Status In review); Template and Rules R1 U8 and the run overlay of the Work Package.
impact: If the documents are revised at approval, the rule IDs, the field list and the messages are re-checked; the split, the lanes and the dependencies do not change.
